PREFACE.


AT  last  the  tenth  and  final  volume  of  The  Guiding
Symptoms  is  completed,  and  the  promise  made  to
Dr.  Hering,  shortly  before  his  death,  and  subsequently  to  the
homoeopathic  profession,  that  the  literary  executors  would
finish  the  colossal  work,  is  fulfilled.  Too  much  cannot  be  said
in  praise  of  the  assiduity  and  faithfulness  of  Drs.  Raue,
Knerr  and  Mohr  in  the  execution  of  their  editorial  labors,
covering  a  period  of  nearly  a  dozen  years.  And  to  Walter  E.
Hering  belongs  the  credit  of  furnishing  the  means  for  the
mechanical  execution  of  his  father's  chef-d^oeuvre.

It  now  remains  for  the  homoeopathic  profession,  for  whose
weal  the  genius  and  fifty  years'  labor  of  Dr.  Constantine  Hering
were  ungrudgingly  given,  to  receive  the  completed  work,  and
use  it,  as  intended  by  its  projector,  for  the  healing  of  the
nations.

THERESE  HERING.

Philadelphia,  October  31,  1891.
